Items.Authors: James J. D. Luis, Juan Paolo L. G. Barrios, David F. Buscher, Michelle J. Creech-Eakman, Emma Floyd, Christopher A. Haniff, Andres Olivares, Jeffrey C. Mason, Chris Salcido, Rafael Santoro, John S. Young
Items.Title: Full-system performance verification results for the Magdalena Ridge Observatory Interferometer’s first two beamlines
Items.Abstract: First stellar fringes at the Magdalena Ridge Observatory Interferometer (MROI) were achieved in July 2025 using a 7.9 m baseline. We have measured the optical performance of the full individual beamlines and aspects of the system as a whole. In this paper we describe the current performance of the MROI in terms of key metrics that typically limit the sensitivity of interferometric measurements, such as static wavefront error, optical throughput, beam alignment jitter/drift and piston jitter. We highlight the remaining issues that we hope to overcome to reach the predicted limiting magnitude of our first science combiner, FOURIER, of 13 in the H band.

Items.Authors: Jacob Trzaska, Amit Ashok
Items.Title: Fundamental limits to wavefront sensing with resolved guide stars
Items.Abstract: We present fundamental limits to wavefront sensing when the telescope's guide star is partially resolved (such as a laser guide star) and the adaptive optics-corrected optical field is weakly aberrated, i.e., we are operating in the "high-Strehl regime." Illustrative simulation examples are shown for the Giant Magellan telescope, where we investigate the minimally achievable phase and amplitude reconstruction errors and methods for saturating the respective limits.

Items.Authors: Julie A. Crooke, Francesco Bordi, Justin Yoshida, Taylor Mize, Elliott Tibor, Leah Sobel, Paul Geithner
Items.Title: Funding scenarios for NASA Astrophysics flagships
Items.Abstract: This paper focuses on one flagship lesson observed to understand the severity of its impact enabling project managers to deliver the development of missions on cost and on schedule. This lesson is the funding profile and funding mechanism. These two synergistic funding characteristics enable all other lessons to be successful or can doom a mission even if all of the other lessons are carried out in the best prescriptive way possible.   We focus on funding methods for NASA compared to those of the DoD. We then provide hybrid NASA-DoD alternative funding methods that builds on past lessons while providing stakeholders the controls they need. We provide analyses of all methods present alternative solutions.

Items.Authors: Hong-yu Jin, Qi Feng, Hui Wang, Hong-fei Zhang, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Gain Measurement and Uncertainty Analysis Using Fe55 X-ray Sources and Photon Transfer Curves
Items.Abstract: Gain, defined as the average number of electrons generated by incident photons per digital number (DN) unit at the output stage of a CCD-detector, constitutes a critical performance metric. The two mainstream characterization methods are Radioisotope Method and Photon Transfer Curve (PTC) Method. Comparatively, The PTC method offers faster testing speeds, while the radioisotope method achieves higher measurement accuracy.   We design an experimental setup for gain measurement based our test camera. In the Fe⁵⁵ source test, a Dewar lid with an internally installed Fe⁵⁵ source and robotic arm is used. In the PTC test, a glass-equipped Dewar lid is employed, placed at one end of the light-tight box, while an adjustable uniform light source is positioned at the other end.  We employ both techniques to measure the gain of a CCD290-99 camera and conduct a comparison with systematic uncertainty quantification.

Items.Authors: Xue Cheng, Yonghe Chen, Yutian Fu
Items.Title: Gain measurement method for CMOS detectors based on a modified photon transfer curve
Items.Abstract: The Earth 2.0 (ET) mission requires extreme image quality and photometric stability from its scientific CMOS detector, relying on precise photon transfer curve (PTC) gain calibration. Traditional PTC methods ignores nonlinear response and fixed-pattern noise, which introduces systematic errors—especially under low-light conditions and across the full dynamic range.  To overcome this, we propose an improved PTC-based gain calculation method. A highly stable monochromatic light source first calibrates the nonlinear response, enabling a pre-correction that removes associated bias. Pixel-level temporal variance analysis is also applied to suppress fixed-pattern noise in PTC fitting.  Simulations and experiments confirm that this method significantly improves detector characterization confidence and offers more accurate gain results. The approach provides a reliable theoretical foundation for developing and evaluating ultra-high-precision space imaging systems.

Items.Authors: Akito Kutsumi
Items.Title: Geant4 simulation of magnet diverter for the wide field view X-ray monitor on HiZ-GUNDAM
Items.Abstract: Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs) are transient phenomena that release energy on the order of 10^52 ergs. The HiZ-GUNDAM project is a future satellite mission aimed at contributing to multi-messenger astronomy and early universe exploration through observations of GRBs. The HiZ-GUNDAM satellite operates in a sun-synchronous orbit to satisfy the temperature requirements of MONSTER. However, this orbit includes the auroral oval and the South Atlantic Anomaly, where many electrons exist. These electrons and their secondary particles increase the background. In the auroral oval, where electron flux is particularly high, for efficient detection by EAGLE, address the electron background with (i) choosing the thickness and material of the EAGLE housing wall, and (ii) the installation of a magnet diverter that prevents electron incidence on the detector by Lorentz force. In this talk, we report on progress of electron background estimation and countermeasure studies using Geant4 simulations.

Items.Authors: Peter M. Thompson, Hugo Chiquito
Items.Title: GMT finite element analysis: state space versus second order form
Items.Abstract: Finite element models are routinely used to design and analyze telescope structures and optical mechanical subsystems. Computational time saving methods are described for both temporal and frequency domain analysis. The standard practice in the telescope design community is to convert the second order model to first order state space form. The preference described here is to stay with the second order form, where for high order problems the computational time can be reduced from hours to minutes, even seconds. These methods are documented here for the wider telescope community

Items.Authors: Timothy Chin, Zhemin Cai, Ali Ghari Zadeh, Jonathan Moller, Dylan Simpfendorfer, Helen McGregor, Yizheng Wang, Jon Lawrence
Items.Title: GNAO AOB: mechanical design of an adaptive optics bench for Gemini North
Items.Abstract: Gemini North Adaptive Optics (GNAO) is a next generation AO system for the 8-metre Gemini North telescope, replacing the existing Altair AO system. The GNAO Adaptive Optics Bench (AOB) will be installed on port 4 of the instrument support structure and houses the deformable mirror and wavefront sensors. AOB will serve to enable GLAO and LTAO within a corrected field of view of 2 arcmin. GNAO is being designed in tandem with the downstream instrument GIRMOS and is planned to go on sky at the same time. The wavefront sensing path includes a laser guide star camera which supports 4 lasers in a 30 arcsec asterism as well as two natural guide star cameras to provide tip tilt and slow focus corrections.    This paper presents the overall mechanical design of the AOB, details on the support structure that houses the electronics cabinets and analysis of the thermal management of the electronics.

Items.Authors: Gwyneth Lannon, Jeffrey Chilcote, Joel Burke, Vincent Chambouleyron, Clarissa R. Do Ó, Jennifer Dunn, Matthew Engstrom, Joeleff Fitzsimmons, Oyku Galvan, Randall Hamper, Dan Kerley, Quinn M. Konopacky, Bruce Macintosh, Christian Marois, Teo Mocnik, Jayke S. Nguyen, Dillon Peng, Saavidra Perera, Brian Sands, Dmitry Savransky, Nicole Wolff
Items.Title: GPI 2.0: detector status and potential new data analysis method for the Gemini Planet Imager
Items.Abstract: The Gemini Planet Imager (GPI) is a facility-class high-contrast imaging instrument designed for the direct detection and characterization of exoplanets. Following its time at the Gemini South Observatory, it is currently undergoing an upgrade to GPI 2.0. Among the systems receiving an upgrade is GPI’s integral field spectrograph (IFS). Since GPI’s removal from Gemini South, the detector in its IFS has deteriorated considerably, and has been replaced as part of the upgrade. This paper will present an account of the old detector’s deterioration from 2014 (the start of GPI’s time at Gemini South) through 2025 and, if available, preliminary performance of the new detector. We will also explore a potential new data analysis method which would allow us to take advantage of the new detector’s increased capabilities.

Items.Authors: Yan Li, Xinyu Yao, Jian Ge, Jianqing Cai, Pengjun Zhang, Congcong Zhang
Items.Title: Ground-based simulation and validation of GSENSE 1081BSI CMOS detectors for ultra-high-precision photometry in the Earth 2.0 Space Mission
Items.Abstract: The Earth 2.0 (ET) space mission requires ultra-high photometric precision (~84 ppm) to detect Earth-like planets around Sun-like stars via the transit method. This paper presents a ground-based simulation experiment designed to evaluate whether the GSENSE 1081BSI CMOS detectors can meet the mission’s photometric performance requirements.The evaluation focused on three key performance metrics: long-term photometric precision, temporal stability, and the ability to recover injected 84 ppm transit signals of Earth 2.0s. Simulated transit events were introduced into the data to directly assess detection capability at the required precision level. The results demonstrate that the GSENSE 1081BSI detectors satisfy the photometric performance re

Items.Authors: Jonas Reiffers, Thomas Bechteler, Andreas Lederhuber, Benjamin Mican, Nandini Satpathy
Items.Title: Hardware development of NewAthena WFI power conditioning module
Items.Abstract: The Wide Field Imager (WFI) is one of the two focal-plane instruments aboard the NewAthena X-ray observatory, the European Space Agency’s second Large-class mission. Scheduled for launch in 2038, NewAthena will operate from the Lagrange point L1, conducting observations in the X-ray energy range between 0.2 keV and 15 keV. The Power Conditioning Module (PCM) is part of the Detector Electronics (DE) of the NewAthena WFI. The primary function of the PCM is to generate the supply voltages for the Front-End Electronics (FEE) of the Camera Head (CH). The PCM represents a critical component for the Camera Head’s performance, as any disturbance in the supply voltages can affect the scientific data or even lead to damage to the sensor or the control ASICs of the CH. To advance the development of the PCM, a prototype was developed. This paper describes the hardware design of the PCM prototype that has already been manufactured.

Items.Authors: Alexis Carlotti, Laurent Jocou, Stéphane Curaba, Steven Martos, Edgard Renault, David Le Mignant, Kjetil Dohlen, Jean-François Sauvage, Charlotte Bond, Arthur Vigan, Mickael Bonnefoy
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: from design trade-offs to prototypes of the high-contrast capability
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first light, adaptive optics assisted,  near-IR integral field spectrograph for the ELT. It covers a spectral range from 800nm to 2450nm with resolving powers from 3000 to 7000 and spatial sampling of 25mas and 6mas. It can operate in two adaptive optics modes - SCAO (including a high contrast capability) and MCAO. The project is resuming its final design phase after a rescope design phase in 2025. The high-contrast (HC) system will enable observations of exoplanets and disks as close as 30mas from the star, and will transmit light from 1250nm up to 2450nm. At 200mas, it will enable the detection of companions displaying a 1e-6 flux ratio (or lower) with the star, using post processing techniques such as ADI, SDI and spectral cross-correlation. We will present an updated view of the system and a new estimation of the contrast limit, as well as results obtained in the laboratory with two testbeds built to prototype both the ZELDA WFS and the overall HC system.

Items.Authors: Johan D. Floriot, Edgard Renault, Kjetil Dohlen, Jean-François Sauvage, Zalpha Challita, William Bon, Anne Bonnefoi, Alexandre Bozier, Anne Costille, David Le Mignant, Rémi Lamble
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: SCAOS design and development plan after rescope
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first light, adaptive optics assisted, near-IR integral field spectrograph for the ELT. It covers a spectral range from 800nm to 2450nm with resolving powers from 3000 to 7000 and spatial sampling of 25mas and 6mas. It can operate in two adaptive optics modes - SCAO (including a high contrast capability) and MCAO. The project is resuming its final design phase after a rescope design phase in 2025.  The updated SCAOS optomechanical design will be presented and discussed. We will also introduce our staggered SCAOS development strategy and detail the design and analysis for each of the modules that we intend to develop and test prior to the system integration: pyramid module, low order adaptive optics loop, ADC module, derotator.

Items.Authors: Salvador Cuevas, Mamadou Ndiaye, Arthur Vigan, Paula Betancourt Esparza, Luis A. Martinez Hernandez, Leonardo Garcés, Carolina Keiman, Beatriz Sanchez, Luis Alvarez-Nuñez
Items.Title: High contrast high resolution integral field spectroscopy with GTC/FRIDA for the study of gas giant exoplanets
Items.Abstract: We explore the potential of FRIDA, on the Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC), to study young gas giant exoplanets. FRIDA is an imager and integral field spectrograph (IFS) which will operate in the near-infrared (0.9-25m) in concert with GTCAO, the adaptive optics (AO) system of GTC. The instrument provides three pixel/spaxel scales: 10, 20, and 40 mas. In its IFS mode, FRIDA features two resolutions: (i) medium (R1500-4000) in the z, J ,H, K bands and (ii) high (R30000) in H and K bands. Additionally, FRIDA exhibits high-contrast capabilities in both imaging and IFS. Among the wide range of science cases, FRIDA is expected to observe young gas giant planets thanks to the combination of the AO corrected beam, coronagraphs, and high-spectral resolution IFS. With its IFS data cube and cross-correlation techniques, FRIDA should be able to identify the presence of molecules in the atmosphere of exoplanets.

Items.Authors: Emanuele Taralli, Sven Visser, Roland Den Hartog, Paul Van der Hulst
Items.Title: High-accuracy cryogenic thermometry via Mott variable-range hopping for Athena/X-IFU
Items.Abstract: We present a compact calibration method for cryogenic NTC thermistors based on the Mott variable-range hopping (MVRH) model, providing an accurate resistance–temperature relation from 40 mK to 40 K. By fitting R(T) with only a few coefficients and inverting it through a truncated Puiseux expansion, the method enables reliable temperature extraction from measured resistance values. Applied to RuO₂ and Ge sensors, it achieves relative residuals ≤1–1.7%, outperforming common polynomial or exponential calibrations while avoiding instability at low temperature. The approach remains robust for sparse datasets and ensures consistent calibration across multiple cryogenic stages. This physically grounded framework is well suited for space instruments requiring precise thermometry, such as the Athena X-IFU Focal Plane Assembly.

Items.Authors: Ross Donnachie, Johan Schoeman
Items.Title: High-fidelity digital IIR filter design for group-delays
Items.Abstract: Presented is the extension of analogue filter design technique to consider digital IIR implementation details. The precision of the binary number system is used to inform the fidelity requirements of the filter’s response. Achieved is a high-fidelity all-pass IIR digital filter design process that has guaranteed convergence and considers implementation characteristics. Such IIR filter networks could replace the Fourier convolution implementations of LTI systems and offer lower resource requirements. Within de-dispersion processes this would raise the ceiling for both real-time processing and search survey efforts.

Items.Authors: Matthew Heine, Catherine E. Grant, Marshall W. Bautz, Beverly J. LaMarr, Eric D. Miller, Michael Hubbard, David Hall, Emanuele Perinati, Steven W. Allen, Artem Poliszczuk, Dan Wilkins, Fabio Gastaldello, Silvano Molendi, Ralph Kraft, Gerrit Schellenberger
Items.Title: High-statistics simulations of NewAthena WFI background using Geant4
Items.Abstract: The observation of hot gas structures is one science goal of the Wide Field Imager (WFI) on ESA’s NewAthena X-ray observatory. Because the measurement of these faint diffuse sources is limited by background from cosmic ray particle interactions within the instrument, understanding and reducing this background is critical. To this end, we employ a two-pronged approach, performing high-fidelity Geant4 simulations on both detailed, realistic geometry models as well as complementary simple geometry models. The former can reveal subtle sensitivities of background to details of the instrument design. The latter allows for fast iteration, useful in guiding and understanding the larger simulations. We show how we leverage resources at the Massachusetts Green High Performance Computing Center (MGHPCC) to achieve simultaneously high throughput and fast time to result. We discuss our recent results, which are applicable to not only WFI, but also other X-ray missions.

Items.Authors: Dhiraj Gupta, Andrea Bianco, Michele Frangiamore, Davide Giughello, Laura Schreiber, Eric Stadler, Emiliano Diolaiti
Items.Title: Holographic diffuser for future applications in astronomical instrumentation
Items.Abstract: Volume Holographic Optical Elements (VHOEs) are specialized components that use recorded interference patterns to shape light wavefronts and they could find applications in modern astronomical instruments where conventional optics cannot easily handle. In adaptive optics (AO) for telescopes, pyramid wavefront sensors need dynamic beam modulation for sensitivity, making the system susceptible to misalignment. In this paper, we present innovative VHOEs that specifically address these challenges. We developed a volume holographic diffuser that offers static wavefront modulation, which can reduce alignment sensitivity in a pyramid AO sensor. This single diffractive element achieves the required small scattering angle with higher diffraction efficiency, meeting the design goals for next-generation astronomical instruments.

Items.Authors: Jose Schiappacasse Ulloa, Laura Magrini, Anna Brucalassi, Sofia Randich, Letizia Caito, Enrico Giro, Marco Riva
Items.Title: HRMOS: Initial development of the exposure time calculator
Items.Abstract: We present the Exposure Time Calculator (ETC) currently under development for HRMOS, the High-Resolution Multi-Object Spectrograph. The HRMOS ETC delivers quantitative predictions of instrument performance across a wide range of observational setups and environmental conditions, enabling accurate estimates of signal-to-noise ratios and exposure times. As a result, it plays a central role throughout the project lifecycle—from guiding instrument design and optimisation to supporting the preparation and planning of scientific observations. We outline the ETC framework, its implementation strategy, and its relevance for maximising the scientific return of HRMOS.

Items.Authors: Ivan Agostinelli, Alessandro Di Filippo, Lorenzo Paonni, Mauro Centrone, Marco Faccini
Items.Title: Hybrid AI optimization for sensorless adaptive optics
Items.Abstract: This work presents an AI-augmented, fully sensorless adaptive optics (AO) framework designed to overcome atmospheric turbulence and reduce the computational burden of real-time correction. The system builds upon ZARA, a metaheuristic wavefront-optimization algorithm that iteratively adjusts Zernike coefficients using a Fourier-based image-quality metric. To accelerate convergence, a lightweight neural pre-conditioner provides a coarse estimate of the corrected point-spread function, narrowing the solution space explored by ZARA. A downstream local optimization module further refines the output through fine-tuning. This three-stage architecture improves robustness, accuracy, and convergence speed, offering a flexible and generalizable closed-loop AO strategy.

Items.Authors: Pierpaolo Merola, Marina Vela Nunez, Vladimiro Noce, Mauro Focardi, Luca Carbonaro, Edoardo Rossi, Simone Chiarucci, Marianna Michelagnoli, Elisabetta Giani, Gianluca Marotta
Items.Title: ICU to TCU interface emulator for the ARIEL Telescope Assembly thermal-vacuum test: hardware and communication logic
Items.Abstract: To read telemetry and command the actuators of the ARIEL Telescope Assembly during thermal-vacuum chamber tests, an Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) has been developed to interface with the Telescope Control Unit (TCU). Nominal communication with the TCU is achieved using an Arduino Due board and a low-voltage differential signaling module housed in a dedicated enclosure. The connection between the EGSE and the TCU relies on a differential-signal interface built on the SPI protocol. As a first step, the communication channel was tested using a second mirrored system capable of receiving commands and returning simulated responses. The final system was assembled and tested using the full TCU simulator at the INAF - Arcetri Astrophysics Observatory. A dedicated communication manager was required to schedule tasks, avoid conflicts, and meet the test requirements.

Items.Authors: Marina Vela Nuñez, Pierpaolo Merola, Vladimiro Noce, Mauro Focardi, Luca Carbonaro, Edoardo Rossi, Simone Chiarucci, Marianna Michelagnoli, Elisabetta Giani, Gianluca Marotta
Items.Title: ICU to TCU interface emulator for the ARIEL Telescope Assembly thermal-vacuum test: software and graphical user interface
Items.Abstract: This paper presents the software modules developed for the “ARIEL ICU–TCU Interface Emulator” (EGSE), designed to support the thermal-vacuum (TVAC) test campaign of the Telescope Assembly of ESA’s ARIEL mission. The emulator implements the ICU–TCU communication link, enabling decoding of telemetry packets, telecommand handling, and the monitoring and control of the TCU during test operations. The GUI provides an integrated environment for configuration, real-time visualization, actuator motion control, telemetry supervision, and automated test procedures. The system was validated first with a data-packet simulator and later with the full TCU simulator at INAF-Arcetri. The emulator enhances test execution efficiency, data accessibility, and provides a scalable framework for future operational procedures.

Items.Authors: David Rodríguez Muñoz, Samuel Sordo Ibañez, Carlos Colodro, Jose Carlos Sanluis Leal, Gara Ramos, Luis Guirado Fuentes, Pablo González de Chaves, Xana Delpueyo Español, Álex Oscoz, Jose Alonso Burgal, Alfonso Ynigo Rivera
Items.Title: Impact of pointing jitter on high-precision photometry for exoplanet detection
Items.Abstract: The Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (IAC) is currently working on the development of IACSAT, which is expected to become the first satellite of the IAC’s future space observatory. IACSAT will be capable of performing high-precision photometry in the VNIR and SWIR bands, primarily aimed at confirming Earth-like exoplanets located within the habitable zone of red dwarf stars.  For high-precision photometry using two-dimensional sensors, pointing stability is critical in order to reduce the impact of detector non-uniformity. This work presents a study of the impact of pointing jitter on photometric performance, including both simulation results and laboratory experiments to validate the proposed mitigation strategies and performance models.

Items.Authors: Been Yeo, Jiwoo Lee, Seonghwan Choi, Kyohoon Ahn
Items.Title: Implementation of an adaptive optics system for free-space optical communication-based quantum key distribution
Items.Abstract: This study aims to implement an adaptive optics (AO) system for free-space optical (FSO) communication-based quantum key distribution (QKD). The exponential increase in data generated by space telescopes and satellites necessitates high-speed and secure data transfer in satellite-ground links. However, atmospheric turbulence causes severe wavefront distortion and beam spreading, drastically reducing coupling efficiency. To ensure stable links, we developed a real-time AO system for an FSO-QKD system. The system measures wavefronts using a Shack-Hartmann Wavefront Sensor with a 19x19 lenslet array and corrects distortion using a Deformable Mirror with 308 actuators (20x20 actuators array). The closed-loop control algorithm uses Zernike polynomials to analyze and minimize aberrations. We have validated the system's performance in a laboratory environment and plan on-sky performance verification using the 1 m telescope at the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute (KASI).

Items.Authors: Solange V. Ramírez, Stephen C. Hope
Items.Title: Implementing a documentation library for MIRMOS
Items.Abstract: We describe the implementation of a documentation library for the Magellan InfraRed Multi-Object Spectrograph (MIRMOS) development team. The need for a unified documentation library was identified as a priority for the MIRMOS project very early into concept development phase. The implementation process started with a definition of use cases and requirements that resulted in a tool choice and subsequent implementation. The library now hosts hundreds of documents; it is widely used by our team and supports our document release process. In this paper, we describe the process of implementation of the document library to support our documentation management plan, as well as a description of the library, some of its most used functionality and some usage statistics. Our implementation is a low-cost solution for a mid-scale instrument team.

Items.Authors: Friederike Wolff, Giulia Alemanno, Emmanuel Marcq, Séverine Robert, Luisa Maria Lara, Andreas Nathues, Vanderlei Cunha Parro, Sandrine Bertran, Justin Erwin, Gisbert Peter, Benjamin Lustrement, Eddy Neefs, Roderick De Cock, Till Hagelschuer, Lisa Hafemeister, Jose Maria Castro, Pablo Gutierrez-Marques, Simone Del Togno
Items.Title: Implementing the VenSpec consortium: from concept to hardware, lessons learned from phase b of the EnVision Mission to Venus
Items.Abstract: VenSpec is a spectrometer consortium aboard ESAs EnVision mission to Venus that sets out to uncover the mysteries of Venus from the surface to the upper atmosphere. Initiated by a the scientifically driven determination to create an overarching science team that spans multiple European institutions to understand geologically coupled phenomena, a consortium has been set up to enable this specific scientific goal. This leads to strong integration in the domains of science, engineering, testing and operations. The structure of this consortium is fully tailored this particular goal and implemented to ensure organizational overhead for all stakeholder is limited to the minimum. This paper describes the status of the project after completion of Phase B and describes the established formal processes as well as the encountered challenges.

Items.Authors: Andres M. Olivares, Chris Salcido, Rafael Santoro, Ian Schofield, Michelle Creech-Eakman, Juan Altamirano, James Luis, Sabrina Orban, Tommaso Marchiori
Items.Title: In-situ integration of the Second Unit Telescope of the Magdalena Ridge Observatory Interferometer (MROI)
Items.Abstract: The Unit Telescope (UT) for the Magdalena Ridge Observatory (MROI) is composed of four major hardware components: The Unit Telescope Mount (UTM), Enclosure, Optics and the Fast Tip Tilt System (FTTS). Integration of the UT started in 2023 when the UTM arrived and its Assembly, Integration and Verification activities began. Critical activities included: installation at the Maintenance Facility, integration and alignment of the Optics and Wave Front Sensor (WFS) and finally the complete optical alignment. End-to-end UTM Site Acceptance Tests (SAT) were performed. Subsequent activities included receiving and integrating the FTTS. With the arrival and assembly of the Enclosure, the last component of the UT was ready for integration on a dedicated concrete pier. We report here the differences between the integration of the UTs, errors made and what we have learned.

Items.Authors: Thomas Berkefeld, Reiner Volkmer, Matthias Schubert, Felix Krämer, Miguel Esteves Perez, Manuel Collados Vera
Items.Title: Instrumentation upgrades to the 1.5m GREGOR German Solar Telescope
Items.Abstract: In 2026, The 1.5m German Solar Telescope GREGOR will receive three major upgrades: CRISP, a dual etalon-based imaging spectro-polarimeter on permanent loan from the 1m Swedish Solar Telescope SST, an upgraded off-limb / prominence adaptive optics system, and an additional third channel working at 770nm for the infrared spectro-polarimeter GRIS. In addition, a new light distribution system will be installed in 2026 / 2027. We will show and discuss the details.

Items.Authors: Pierre-Louis Mayeur, Thierry Fusco, Nicolas Vedrenne, Jean-François Sauvage, Cyril Petit, Romain Fetick, Pierre Guiot
Items.Title: INTERSTELLAR a high angular, spectral, and temporal resolution instrument for LEO observation with the PROVIDENCE-2.5m Telescope: system analysis and design
Items.Abstract: ONERA – The French Aerospace Laboratory has launched the PROVIDENCE project to develop a 2.5m-class telescope for Space Domain Awareness (SDA) by 2028. The telescope, optimized for High Angular Resolution with Adaptive Optics, will enable detection, identification, and monitoring of LEO and GEO objects. We expect this unique Optical Ground Station in Europe to trigger international collaboration. The development of the first light instrument for multispectral LEO satellite imaging is led by ONERA and the first design steps are ongoing in order to achieve an instrument able to autonomously acquire High Resolute data. We discuss the system analysis and the preliminary design of the instrument.

Items.Authors: Christian Ketchazo, Marion Baumann, Cyrille Delisle, Sophie Derelle, Benoît Horeau, Edouard Huard, Michel Lortholary, Vincent Moreau, Salima Mouzali, Patrick Mulet, Thierry Orduna, Thibault Pichon, Lena Provost, Samuel Ronayette, Olivier Tellier, Olivier Gravrand, Adrien Lamourre, Olivier Boulade
Items.Title: Intrapix: a test bench dedicated to the measurement of intra-pixel response of astrophysics detectors. Validation campaign and early results on an ALFA 2Kx2K SWIR detector
Items.Abstract: The Intrapixel response is an important parameter to know as it can affect the accuracy of photometric and galaxies shape measurements in astrophysics. At CEA-IRFU, a test bench called “Intrapix” has been specifically designed for this measurement.   In this paper, a description of the test bench will be presented and the measurement techniques will be exposed. The main part of the paper will focus on the validation activities. The measurements results derived from the ASTEROID detector will be shared and discussed. A section will be dedicated to the tests carried on an ALFA detector.

Items.Authors: Mingfu Shao, Jiaben Lin, Liyue Tong, Hui Wang
Items.Title: JW-FlareNet: a three-decade, continuously updated solar image dataset for AI-driven flare forecasting
Items.Abstract: We introduce a image dataset designed for solar flare forecasting, integrating full-disk line-of-sight photospheric magnetograms and co-aligned continuum intensity images from the MDI/SOHO and HMI/SDO, covering the period from 1998 to 2025. The dataset provides flare activity annotations for solar active regions based on authoritative flare catalogs. It extended temporal coverage across nearly three solar cycles and a self-growing capability supported by an automated pipeline that daily retrieves the latest magnetogram and integrates flare lists. All images undergo uniform preprocessing and are spatiotemporally correlated with flare events. This dataset serves as a foundational resource for space weather research, particularly in developing AI-based flare prediction models. As the image dataset for flare prediction combining multi-decadal coverage with auto-updating capacity, it is positioned to become a key benchmark for next-generation automated space weather forecasting systems.

Items.Authors: Ioannis Apergis, Leonidas Asimakoulas, Daniel Bayliss, Paul Chote, James McCormac, Morgan A. Mitchell
Items.Title: Lab and on-sky testing of Andor Toran CMOS camera for astronomical applications
Items.Abstract: We present laboratory and on-sky performance results for the Toran, a new scientific CMOS camera from Oxford Instruments Andor, tested in its Low Noise (LN) and High Well Capacity (HWC) modes. Laboratory measurements show read noise of 1.07 e⁻ (LN) and 2.79 e⁻ (HWC), dark-signal non-uniformities of 0.076 e⁻ and 0.173 e⁻, and well depths of 15,700 e⁻ and 50,100 e⁻, corresponding to dynamic ranges of 83.39 and 85.05 dB. The detector exhibits excellent linearity (>99.8%) and low PRNU (<0.08%). Dark current is extremely low at 0.001 e⁻ pix⁻¹ s⁻¹ at 0 °C. On-sky tests at the TWenty Inch Survey Telescope (TWIST) at the Roque de Los Muchachos observatory in La Palma, Spain, show that HWC becomes camera-noise limited for faint stars due to its higher read noise, while LN consistently delivers superior photometric precision. These results highlight Toran as a strong candidate for high-precision time-domain astronomy.

Items.Authors: Marcelo Said Tala Pinto, Marshall Johnson, Julia Brady, Xavier Lesley, Jonathan Crass, Allie Renshaw, Michael Engelman, Brian Sands, Daniel Pappalardo, Christian Schwab, Julian Stürmer, Dane Zielinski-Nicolson, Matheus J. Castro, Stanimir Letchev, Thomas Legero, Ondrej Kitzler, Jacob Pember, Richard Pogge, Justin R. Crepp, Andrew Bechter, Eric Bechter
Items.Title: Laboratory characterization of iLocater
Items.Abstract: We present the latest laboratory characterization and optimization of the iLocater diffraction-limited, high-resolution near-infrared spectrograph. Our work focuses on measuring and optimizing optical performance, spectral resolution, and instrument stability. An iterative OpticStudio-guided focusing procedure improved optical alignment and spot quality across the detector. Using a Fabry–Pérot etalon and UNe lamps, we assessed resolving power and short- and long-term stability under controlled environmental conditions. We report updated optical and thermal performance metrics and instrument readiness for on-sky commissioning.

Items.Authors: Yang Gao, Wen Chen, Xuliang Duan, Kun Chen, Yingquan Yang, Rong Shu, Junfei Li, Yonghe Chen, Jian Ge
Items.Title: Layered thermal design for ultra-precision photometry of the Earth 2.0 space mission
Items.Abstract: The Earth 2.0 (ET) space mission required to detect Earth-sized exoplanets via the transit method demands exceptional thermal stability. The mission's thermal control system must counteract environmental heating flux and significant internal heat generated by equipment. In order to achieve this goal, a layered thermal design method has been applied, with a precisely thermal controlled optical bench made of low thermal expansion coefficient C-SiC material, a thermally control shield around the optical bench, flexible supporting truss isolating platform thermal flux, and a big multi-layer sun-shield resisting against the direct solar flux. This paper introduce the structural and thermal design of the spacecraft, focusing on the ultra-stable thermal design as well as simulation and test with a cut-off optical bench.

Items.Authors: András Péter Joó, Knud Jahnke, Bendegúz Koncz, Rebeka Gyöngyi Kiss, Örs Hunor Detre, Gyula Zilizi, Zsolt Bagoly, István Rácz, Sándor Pintér, István Horváth, L. Viktor Tóth
Items.Title: LED-based calibration for the THESEUS InfraRed Telescope: calibration unit design concept
Items.Abstract: The InfraRed Telescope (IRT) on the THESEUS ESA M7 mission candidate requires precise radiometric calibration to enable accurate localisation and spectroscopy of high-energy transients. We present the conceptual design of the IRT’s LED-based Calibration Unit, developed to provide highly uniform and temporally stable illumination across five NIR bands, compliant with tight volume and critical alignment requirements. The design builds upon the heritage and demonstrated in-flight performance of the Euclid NISP Calibration Unit, offering valuable guidance for stability, packaging, and long-term behaviour of infrared LEDs in space. The resulting concept targets sub-percent radiometric accuracy, supporting THESEUS’s infrared measurement goals and advancing future space-based NIR instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Arno P. Schoenmakers
Items.Title: Lessons learned: Enhancing synchronization in the hardware and software development for the LOFAR upgrade
Items.Abstract: The Low-Frequency Array (LOFAR), one of the worlds largest radio telescopes, underwent significant modernization after its original construction between 2009 and 2012. This update required a comprehensive overhaul of its ageing signal processing technology and on-board software systems. A key challenge emerged due to the differing development approaches of the hardware teams, who worked in traditional iterative cycles spanning up to several months, and the software teams, who used Agile Scrum with rapid, three-weekly iterations. This caused planning misalignment and other issues during the project. To reconcile this we attempted to better synchronize the planning cycle. This improved collaboration and communication between the various disciplines involved in the development of the LOFAR update.

Items.Authors: Ashtyn Earl, Jamil Fayyad, Todd Charter, Maaike A. van Kooten, Kate Jackson, Jean-Pierre Véran, Homayoun Najjaran
Items.Title: Leveraging machine learning for PWFS reconstruction: bench validation with REVOLT
Items.Abstract: The pyramid wavefront sensor (PWFS) is well known for its sensitivity and is gaining popularity in adaptive optics (AO) systems, but its strong nonlinearity under large wavefront errors limits its dynamic range. Conventional AO systems address this with optical modulation, which linearizes the PWFS response at the cost of sensitivity and added complexity. Machine learning (ML) provides an alternative by reconstructing the PWFS output without modulation, preserving its intrinsic sensitivity. We present a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based reconstructor trained and validated using unmodulated PWFS data from the Research, Experiment, and Validation of adaptive Optics on a Legacy Telescope (REVOLT) platform at NRC Herzberg. Bench testing demonstrates accurate prediction of deformable mirror commands across diverse wavefront conditions, confirming the feasibility of ML-based reconstruction for PWFS. Future work will extend this approach to on-sky operation with REVOLT.

Items.Authors: Man-Yin Leo Lee, Shelley A. Wright, Renate Kupke, Aaron Brown, Jérôme Maire, Reagen Leimbach, Bryson Cale, James Wiley, Chris Johnson, Evan Kress, James Larkin, Nathan Magari, Kenneth Magnone, Eric Wang
Items.Title: Liger at W.M. Keck Observatory: imager optical alignment
Items.Abstract: In the paper, we will present how to align the imager components of liger, a next-generation near-infrared imager and integral field spectrograph (IFS) on the Keck I telescope. The liger imager consists of two off-axis parabolic (OAP) mirrors, a flat fold mirror, a pupil wheel, a filter wheel, a pupil-viewing camera, and the Teledyne Hawaii-2RG detector. We will show the steps to align the imager in a precise level and conduct warm and cold testing and a telescope simulator to verify the quality of our alignment.

Items.Authors: Ren-jie Zhao, Wen-qing Qu, Hao-ran Ma, Yu Ning, Feng Zeng, Hong-fei Zhang, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Low-Noise Readout electronics using high-speed digitalization scheme for MCT Detectors
Items.Abstract: This work focuses on developing a low-noise readout electronics using a high-speed digitalization scheme for Mercury Cadmium Telluride (MCT) infrared focal-plane detectors, which are widely used in astronomical observations due to their high sensitivity and excellent low-temperature performance. To meet the requirements of faint-object imaging, the system employs a 500 kHz pixel readout clock combined with a 20 MHz ADC oversampling architecture. High-speed oversampling allows the readout chain to capture multiple samples within each pixel period, enabling subsequent digital filtering and weighted averaging to effectively reduce temporal noise, suppress quantization and electronic interference, and improve the overall signal-to-noise ratio. The proposed method achieves low-noise readout without sacrificing frame rate, offering a practical solution for high-performance infrared astronomical imaging..

Items.Authors: Ole Streicher, Anastasia Galkin, Simeon Reusch, Clare Worley
Items.Title: Machine-readable data models for robust data curation and release in 4MOST
Items.Abstract: Machine-readable data models are central to ensuring data integrity during 4MOST data curation and release. They provide formal, structured descriptions of complex raw and reduced data, enabling automated validation, consistent quality checks, and reproducible transformations. Within the 4MOST Pre-Release Access Point (4PRAP), these models support reliable coordination across heterogeneous workflows, from commissioning to archival. The poster presents the approach adopted to enforce data integrity using structured, machine-actionable models, illustrating their role in robust data management and preparation of science-ready 4MOST data products.

Items.Authors: Emanuele Taralli, Martin De Wit, Roland Den Hartog, Davide Vaccaro, Pourya Khosropanah
Items.Title: Magnetic and mechanical stability of the Athena X-IFU focal plane assembly: results from the development model
Items.Abstract: We present magnetic-shielding and micro-vibration characterization of the X-IFU FPA Development Model for Athena space telescope. The FPA ensures a stable environment for the TES array at 50 mK using a multi-stage thermal suspension and a CMM–Nb shield. TESs act as sensitive magnetometers via their Fraunhofer-like response to perpendicular fields. Four Helmholtz coils installed inside the cryostat apply controlled AC/DC fields (<200 μT) without magnetizing the CMM. Preliminary results show a shielding factor ≥10⁵ at the detector plane, with the upgraded setup expected to increase this limit. Micro-vibrations in the 100–1000 Hz range are analyzed by correlating accelerometers on T2, thermometers across the FPA, and TES baseline variations. Resonant modes are identified, and their impact on thermal stability, dissipation, and detector noise is assessed to guide optimization of future FPA models.

Items.Authors: Mauro Focardi, Sebastiano Ligori, Anna Maria Di Giorgio, Vito Capobianco, Donata Bonino, Natalia Auricchio, Leonardo Corcione, Vladimiro Noce, Pierpaolo Merola, Marina Vela Nuñez, Simone Chiarucci, Maria Farina, Marianna Michelagnoli, Elisabetta Giani, Gianluca Marotta, Edoardo Rossi, Alessandra Tortora, Luca Serafini, Selene Salvetti, Alessio Pannocchia, Fulvio De Persio, Daniele Brienza, Elisabetta Tommasi Di Vignano, Navin K. Shivapa Kamble, Giovanni Giusi, Andrea Russi, Marius Stoica, Scige Liu, Emanuele Pace, Giampaolo Preti, Benoît Horeau, Michel Berthé, Christophe Cara, José Maria Gomez, Laura Martì, Andrew Caldwell, Paul Eccleston, Alexander Davidson, Rachel Drummond, Gianluca Morgante, Giuseppe Malaguti, Giuseppina Micela, Giovanna Tinetti, Caroline Simpson, Eduardo Medinaceli
Items.Title: Manufacturing and testing the Avionic and Engineering models of the Instrument Control Unit of the ARIEL Mission: an overview of the Unit implementation and verification status following its Critical Design Review
Items.Abstract: ARIEL is the M4 mission of the ESA’s Cosmic Vision 2015-2025 program, whose aim is to chemically characterise by low-resolution transit spectroscopy the atmospheres of over one thousand exoplanets orbiting nearby stars.  ARIEL hosts two scientific instruments, AIRS (ARIEL IR Spectrometer) and FGS (Fine Guidance Sensor) performing spectroscopy and spectro-photometry in the VIS and NIR range. AIRS is managed by an Instrument Control Unit (ICU), a Spacewire/PUS (Packet Utilization Standard) remote terminal, whose architecture and general status will be provided in this paper, including a summary of the main processing tasks implemented on-board its processor, following the closeout of the Critical Design Review (CDR) and the development and testing of the on-board Application SW (ASW) versions for both the Avionic (AVM) and Engineering (EM) models.

Items.Authors: zhemin cai, Ali Ghari Zadeh, Christopher Coote, Timothy Chin, Jonathan Moller, Dylan Simpfendorfer, Helen M. McGregor, Jessica R. Zheng, Jonathon S. Lawrence, Yizheng Wang, Dani Guzman, Esra Kirkac, Cagatay Kirkac, Jake Linden, Michael Goodwin, Nick Cerneaz
Items.Title: Material selection and performance analysis of the GNAO adaptive optical bench system under gravity, thermal, and vibration loads
Items.Abstract: This paper presents a focused material selection and performance assessment for the Gemini North Adaptive Optics (GNAO) bench, a key element of the next-generation AO system for the 8-meter Gemini North telescope. Finite element analysis in Ansys Mechanical examined gravity-vector changes, thermal expansion, and vibration response, while Zemax optical modeling verified that resulting deformations remained within tolerance. Three materials were evaluated: fiber composite, stainless steel, and aluminum. The study found clear trade-offs in stiffness, thermal behavior, and cost. Although composites reduce mass and stainless steel offers high strength, an all-aluminum structure provides the best balance of performance, stability, and cost for the final design.

Items.Authors: Nicolò Azzaroli, Simone Doniselli, Enrico Pinna, Marco Bonaglia
Items.Title: MAVIS: alignment tolerance analysis for the natural guide star wavefront sensor and acquisition camera
Items.Abstract: This work presents a Monte-Carlo alignment tolerance analysis of the Natural Guide Star Wavefront Sensor (NGS WFS) and Acquisition Camera (Acq Cam), key subsystems of the MAVIS instrument for the VLT. The study quantifies residual alignment errors after opto-mechanical integration, examining all relevant degrees of freedom of critical optical components. For the NGS WFS, 1500 MC replicas in 1×1 and 2×2 configurations show that residual Wavefront Error and spot radius stay within requirements. For the Acq Cam, a merit-function optimization minimizes on-axis RMS spot size and evaluates performance at maximum field. Results from 2000 MC replicas confirm compliance even in worst-case conditions. Overall, the analysis validates the robustness of the mechanical design and alignment procedures.

Items.Authors: Andrew W. Kruse, Israel J. Vaughn, Dionne Haynes, Trevor Mendel, Antony Galla, Brent Miszalski, Richard McDermid, Nuwanthika Fernando, Nuria Lorente, Miguel Gonzalez-Bolivar
Items.Title: MAVIS: calibration unit Fabry-Perot etalon design and simulation
Items.Abstract: The MAVIS Spectrograph provides two spatial resolutions and four spectral modes, with spectral resolutions of R ~ 4000-7000 over 370-695 nm or 495-935 nm, R ~ 11000-13000 over 630-880 nm, or R ~14000-15000 over 425-550 nm. The wavelength calibration of the spectrograph is enabled by a combination of natural emission lines and a full-spectrum of Fabry-Perot etalon peaks. The transmission spectrum of the etalon was simulated using a custom software package that incorporates the various effects on the finesse and location of the peaks, including the wavelength-dependent cavity length due to the phase of the dielectric coating. This effect is a crucial factor for evaluating the robustness of wavelength calibration algorithms. This is especially true for the MAVIS calibration, due to the large spectral bands where the phase of the coating varies significantly. Transmission peak thermal stability was modelled using the thermal expansion of the spacer and the dielectric coating layers.

Items.Authors: Matteo Aliverti, Simone Doniselli, Antony Galla, Gaston Gausachs, Brian W. Taylor, Annino Vaccarella, Marco Bonaglia, Mirko Colapietro, Davide Greggio, Luca Marafatto, Enrico pinna, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Maria Bergomi, Valentina Viotto, François Rigaut, David Brodrick, Richard M. McDermid, Jennifer Burgess
Items.Title: MAVIS: FDR mechanical design of the adaptive optics module
Items.Abstract: MAVIS (MCAO Assisted Visible Imager and Spectrograph) is a Multi-Conjugate Adaptive Optics instrument for VLT's UT4, delivering corrected fields of view to a spectrograph, imager, and visiting instrument. Following Final Design Review, we present the Adaptive Optics Module (AOM) mechanical architecture. The optical bench supports post-focal relay optics (ADC, K-mirror derotator, deformable mirrors, selector) and rigidly mounts the calibration unit, guide star modules, and imager. The Overall Mechanical Structure connects to the Nasmyth platform while supporting the spectrograph and providing environmental isolation. We present final design solutions emphasizing the K-mirror system, material selection, and mechanical adhesive selections, with validation through thermoelastic, modal, and structural analyses.

Items.Authors: Mirko Colapietro, Salvatore Savarese, Sergio D'Orsi, Pietro Schipani, Giulio Capasso, Gregory Jolley, Lewis G. Waller, Brian Taylor, Bernardo Salasnich, Elia Costa, David Brodrick, Gaston Gausachs, Stefan Ströbele, Pierre Haguenauer, Matteo Aliverti, Simone Doniselli, Tristan Monnier, Annino Vaccarella, Mark Downing, Dionne Haynes, Antony Galla, Maria Bergomi, Enrico Pinna, Fabio Rossi, Valentina Viotto, Jennifer Burgess, Francois Rigaut, Roger Haynes, Paolo Cerpelloni, Luca Marafatto, Kalyan Radhakrishnan Santhakumari
Items.Title: MAVIS: overview of the control electronics final design
Items.Abstract: MAVIS (the MCAO-Assisted Visible Imager and Spectrograph) is a next-generation instrument for the ESO Very Large Telescope (VLT).  It includes Multi-Conjugate Adaptive Optics (MCAO) module with an advanced Imager and Spectrograph, supported by a dedicated calibration unit. All subsystems are housed within an enclosure to ensure thermal stability throughout the observing night.  The instrument control electronics are housed in eight actively cooled cabinets distributed across three different levels. The control electronics architecture adopts a modular approach that simplifies integration: three PLC CPUs are dedicated to controlling and monitoring all instrument functions, while a fourth CPU is fully dedicated to the Cryo-Vacuum System.  This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the final design of the MAVIS Control Electronics, detailing the architectural choices, subsystem interfaces, control cabinet layout and the implementation of the telemetry, interlock, and safety systems.

Items.Authors: Matteo Aliverti, Mirko Colapietro, Simone Doniselli, Salvatore Savarese, Luca Marafatto, Stefan Ströbele, Gaston Gausachs, Marco Bonaglia, Valentina Viotto, Maria Bergomi, David Brodrick, François Rigaut, Jennifer Burgess
Items.Title: MAVIS: PFR and NGS mechanical prototyping
Items.Abstract: MAVIS (MCAO Assisted Visible Imager and Spectrograph) is a Multi-Conjugate Adaptive Optics instrument for VLT's UT4, delivering corrected fields of view to multiple science channels. Following Final Design Review, we present key prototyping activities for the Post Focal Relay and Natural Guide Star module: deformable mirror alignment system, patrolling stage, and K-mirror assembly.  The DM alignment system employs dummy elements replicating mirror positions, with cable management testing for 8-meter deployment. The patrolling stage was characterized for motion accuracy.  K-mirror prototyping validated wobble, runout, and pupil shift requirements. Tests demonstrated exceptional repeatability, negligible backlash, and tracking performance exceeding specifications. Mirror alignment achieved sub-5-micrometer accuracy with 1-micrometer gravitational deformation. Tests validate design compliance and inform final optimization.

Items.Authors: Eduardo David González Carretero, José M. Delgado-Hernández, Marcos Reyes García-Talavera, Víctor J. Sánchez Béjar, Roberto López-López, Ángel Mato Martínez, Verónica Canto-Caño, Óscar Manuel Tubío Araújo, Icíar Montilla Garcia, José Marco de La Rosa, Ana Belén Nuñez Chico, Fabio Tenegi Sanginés, Roberto Simoes, Afrodisio Vega-Moreno, Jesús Patrón-Recio, Josefina Rosich Minguell, Manuel Luis Aznar
Items.Title: Mechanical design, cryogenic architecture, and telescope integration of the GRANCAIN infrared camera for the Gran Telescopio Canarias
Items.Abstract: GRANCAIN is the new cryogenic near-infrared imager for the J, H, and K bands at the Gran Telescopio Canarias and has reached its operational configuration on the telescope, where it has already produced its first on-sky images with the GTCAO adaptive optics system. The instrument is enclosed in an aluminum cryostat cooled to 50–77 K, ensuring thermal stability for the optical bench that carries the collimator–camera assembly, two cryogenic filter wheels, the cold stop, and a 4-Mpx HAWAII-2 PACE detector. Its mechanical architecture uses athermalized, precision-adjustable mounts to preserve alignment through cooldown, while mixed-material lens cells minimize stress on the optics. A comprehensive metrology and cryogenic testing campaign verified compliance with the required tolerances. The paper also outlines the Nasmyth interface and vibration-control measures. GRANCAIN’s successful deployment enables high-quality NIR imaging at the GTC.

Items.Authors: Hannah Pollek, Gabriele Rodeghiero, John Andrew, Alex Drlica-Wagner, Alessio Taranto, Luca Rosignoli, Aashay Pai, Douglas R. Neill, Travis Lange, Andrew P. Rasmussen, Aaron Roodman, Pierre Antilogus, Alexandre Boucaud, Martin Nordby
Items.Title: Mechanical studies of an additional light baffle for the LSST camera
Items.Abstract: During the commissioning of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, work was performed to identify and mitigate the effects of stray light to minimize impacts that it may have on the Legacy Survey of Space and Time. The detailed Zemax models produced have found that the addition of a mechanical baffle inside the LSST Camera has the potential to mitigate a notable portion of the identified stray light artifacts. This paper presents the mechanical studies regarding feasibility of installing one such baffle near the third lens (L3), and the ideal geometry to maximize benefit to the survey. The primary topics considered are the space limitations and access needed to install it, material and coating possibilities, and potential thermal impacts of this added hardware.
